fix1_timing.note: Latency fits the window with huge margin. Raw sampler is data-dependent in time (the McMurtry timing channel); the constant-time wrapper flattens the variance so timing reveals nothing.

fix2_attacker.note: A neural-net attacker also reads keystrokes with no privacy and is also driven to near chance by the fixed defence, so the leak is not an artifact of the tree model.

fix3_anomalies.injected: sensor shift (+0.15 baseline) and sweat (+-40% slow gain drift)
fix3_anomalies.note: Because the feature is clipped to [0,1] before noising, no anomaly can push the sensitivity past the bound, so eps-DP holds regardless (log-ratio <= eps). Anomalies hurt utility, not the privacy guarantee: the defence still holds.

fix4_mode_transitions.note: A late mode switch leaves edge keystrokes on the loose budget (eps_event up to 16 instead of 1). A guard band that turns the tight budget on a few windows early drives the exposed fraction to zero.
